headline: NHS Doctor Uses AI to Solve Mother's Mystery Illness
meta_description: An NHS doctor turned to Google's Gemini AI to identify a treatable cause behind his mother's severe seizures while hospitalised with Parkinson's Disease.
summary_short: When his mother with Parkinson's lay in hospital having constant fits, an NHS doctor used AI to uncover a likely B6 deficiency—a finding that could change her outcome.
body:
An NHS doctor faced an urgent puzzle when his mother was hospitalised with relentless seizures and a poor prognosis. With limited time and conventional approaches seemingly exhausted, he turned to an unexpected tool: Google's Gemini AI. The artificial intelligence helped him identify a potential underlying cause—a B6 deficiency—that had gone undetected through standard hospital protocols.

The case highlights how AI might assist medical professionals in recognising treatable conditions that could otherwise be overlooked. A B6 deficiency can trigger seizures and is potentially reversible with proper supplementation, offering hope where none seemed available. The doctor's resourcefulness in consulting the technology while his mother was critically ill shows how emerging tools are beginning to support clinical decision-making at crucial moments.

This discovery underscores an emerging role for AI in healthcare: not as a replacement for medical expertise, but as a partner in catching what might otherwise slip through—especially in complex cases where time is running short.

Mother had Parkinson's Disease with constant seizures in hospital
AI identified likely B6 deficiency as underlying cause
B6 deficiency can trigger seizures and may be reversible
